Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: At baseline, 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels were significantly lower in premenopausal women with major depression than in healthy controls.
Sentence: "At baseline, ionized calcium and 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels were significantly lower in women with MDD compared to controls."
Measured as: major depressive disorder (MDD)
Population: Premenopausal women aged 21 to 45 years with major depressive disorder (n=92) and healthy controls (n=44)
Intervention: No intervention; baseline serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D level measured
Comparator: Healthy controls
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 136
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
